## LITERATURE SCAN: Ventral-Visual-Stream-to-MTL Representational Hierarchy & Conjunctive-Code Interference Reduction

### 1. HIERARCHY: posterior=simple features, IT=complex features, perirhinal=higher-arity conjunctions

**ESTABLISHED as a theoretical framework (repeatedly and explicitly stated by its originating group), empirically CONTESTED/SINGLE-STUDY at the neural-gradient level.**

- **Bussey, T.J. & Saksida, L.M. (2007).** "Memory, perception, and the ventral visual–perirhinal–hippocampal stream: thinking outside of the boxes." *Hippocampus*, 17(9), 898–908. PMID 17636546. Foundational statement of a perception-memory continuum: representations become progressively more complex/conjunctive moving anterior along the ventral visual stream (VVS), with perirhinal cortex (PRC) at the apex, and memory/perception are not discretely separated systems but points on this representational continuum.
- **Bussey, T.J., Saksida, L.M., & Murray, E.A. (2005).** "The perceptual-mnemonic/feature conjunction model of perirhinal cortex function." *Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology B*, 58(3–4), 269–282. DOI 10.1080/02724990544000004. PMID 16194969. The named "PMFC model" — explicit claim: PRC stores conjunctions of visual features of complex objects; PRC lesions selectively disrupt discriminations with high "feature ambiguity" (defined below).
- **Cowell, R.A., Bussey, T.J., & Saksida, L.M. (2010).** "The representational–hierarchical view of amnesia: translation from animal to human." *Neuropsychologia*, 48(8), 2251–2261. DOI 10.1016/j.neuropsychologia.2010.02.026. PMID 20206190. Explicit statement (secondary-source confirmed, direct fetch of full text blocked by paywall so treat the specific numeric content as UNVERIFIED): the model formalizes a hierarchy of increasing representational complexity from caudal VVS to PRC and is used to generate testable predictions for human amnesia.
- **Kent, B.A., Hvoslef-Eide, M., Saksida, L.M., & Bussey, T.J. (2016).** "The representational–hierarchical view of pattern separation: not just hippocampus, not just space, not just memory?" *Neurobiology of Learning and Memory*, 129, 99–106. DOI confirmed via ScienceDirect (10.1016/j.nlm.2016.01.006, not independently re-verified — flag as SECONDARY-SOURCE-derived). This is the correct citation matching the task's "Kent et al. 2016" reference (the task description's exact title differs slightly — I could not find a paper titled "Perirhinal cortex representations..." by Kent 2016; this pattern-separation paper is the real Kent/Bussey/Saksida 2016 entry and is likely what was intended — **FLAG: possible title mismatch in the original task, treat with caution**). Explicit claim: defines pattern separation as reducing overlap between similar input patterns to minimize interference among stored representations, and extends the representational-hierarchical view beyond hippocampus/space/episodic memory to any brain region computing over hierarchically-organized representations, including PRC's role in reducing interference among perceptually similar objects.
- **Cowell, R.A., Bussey, T.J., & Saksida, L.M. (2006).** "Why does brain damage impair memory? A connectionist model of object recognition memory in perirhinal cortex." *Journal of Neuroscience*, 26(47), 12186–12197. DOI 10.1523/JNEUROSCI.2818-06.2006. PMCID PMC6675420 (full text retrieved). Direct quote extracted from full text: **"Simple features, labeled A–D, are represented in caudal regions of the VVS. More complex representations of the conjunctions of those features are stored in more rostral regions, with complexity reaching a maximum in perirhinal cortex."** This is the clearest explicit statement of the exact three-tier (posterior-simple / IT-complex / PRC-conjunctive) architecture requested. ESTABLISHED as the theoretical claim of this research program.
- **Cowell, R.A., Bussey, T.J., & Saksida, L.M. (2010).** "Components of recognition memory: dissociable cognitive processes or just differences in representational complexity?" *Hippocampus*, 20(11), 1245–1262. PMID 20882548. Reframes recognition-memory dissociations (familiarity vs recollection) as differences in representational complexity along the same hierarchy rather than distinct cognitive processes — CONTESTED reframing, argued against dual-process memory theory.

**Empirical fMRI/RSA tests of an increasing-conjunctivity gradient:**

- **Erez, J., Cusack, R., Kendall, W., & Barense, M.D. (2016).** "Conjunctive coding of complex object features." *Cerebral Cortex*, 26(5), 2271–2282. DOI 10.1093/cercor/bhv081. PMID 25921583. SINGLE-STUDY finding: using MVPA on fMRI data with artificial multi-part objects, activity patterns throughout the VVS extending into PRC discriminated between identical parts/features combined into different whole-object configurations — i.e., an explicit conjunctive code over and above the sum of feature-level codes, with the effect most pronounced approaching PRC. I could not retrieve exact classification-accuracy or statistical (t/F) values from this paper directly (paywalled; only abstract-level text retrieved) — **UNPINNED at the level of exact numbers in my hands**, though the qualitative gradient claim is clearly stated in the abstract/secondary sources.
- **Martin, C.B., Douglas, D., Newsome, R.N., Man, L.L.Y., & Barense, M.D. (2018).** "Integrative and distinctive coding of visual and conceptual object features in the ventral visual stream." *eLife*, 7, e31873. DOI 10.7554/eLife.31873. (This is the actual paper the task calls "Martin, Douglas, Newsome, Man, Barense eLife 2018" — full text retrieved.) Reports RSA correlations by region: LOC–visual-behavior RDM Kendall's tau-a = 0.045 (p<0.002); PRC–visual-behavior RDM tau-a = 0.052 (p<0.0001); PRC–conceptual-behavior RDM tau-a = 0.036 (p<0.0003); within-object cross-task-context similarity PRC Pearson's r=0.41 (p<0.01), temporal pole r=0.34 (p<0.05). These numbers show PRC representations integrating both visual and conceptual similarity more strongly/more stably than LOC — consistent with, but not a strict single-feature-arity gradient test of, the hierarchy claim. Tag: SINGLE-STUDY, moderate effect sizes (tau≈0.04–0.05 is numerically small though statistically significant — worth flagging that the "gradient" signal in whole-brain RSA is modest in absolute magnitude).
- **Kalava/related:** Barense lab further work — "Activity in perirhinal and entorhinal cortex predicts perceived visual similarities among category exemplars with highest precision" (eLife 2021/2022, PMC9020819) — SINGLE-STUDY, further supports increasing precision of fine-grained (near-conjunctive) similarity coding moving into PRC/entorhinal cortex, not independently pulled for numbers here.

**Electrophysiology / receptive-field-size gradient:** I did NOT find a paper in this scan that directly ties classic IT/PRC receptive-field-size electrophysiology (e.g., Desimone, Tanaka-style RF gradients) into quantitative "feature-complexity vs receptive field size" numbers cited by the Cowell/Bussey/Saksida program. This linkage is asserted qualitatively (larger RFs, more complex/invariant selectivity moving anterior in IT/PRC, classic single-unit literature e.g. Tanaka 1996, Desimone & Ungerleider) but I could not pin an explicit quantitative statement connecting RF size to conjunction arity in a single paper within this scan — **UNPINNED**, flag as a gap in this scan rather than a literature gap per se (could exist in Tanaka 1996 "Inferotemporal cortex and object vision," not directly retrieved here).

### 2. REPLACE OR COEXIST?

**ESTABLISHED (explicit, direct-quote level) — the conjunctive layer COEXISTS with, does not replace, feature-level representations.**

From Cowell, Bussey & Saksida 2006 (J Neurosci, full text): the connectionist model architecture explicitly instantiates two parallel layers — a "feature layer" and a "conjunctive layer" — and **"training proceeds in parallel on the two layers, and recognition performance is determined by averaging the recognition scores elicited by sample and novel stimuli on the two layers."** This is an explicit, quantifiable statement that the model is additive/parallel at the architecture level (both layers persist and jointly determine output) rather than the conjunctive layer overwriting or replacing the feature layer. This directly answers the "feedforward-additive, each level adds a conjunction level, lower levels persist" question: YES, that is exactly how Cowell/Bussey/Saksida instantiate it computationally — each hierarchical level is additive/coexisting, not recoding away the lower level.

The explicit "resolution of feature ambiguity" framing (same paper, and Bartko et al. 2007, and the PMFC model 2005) states the functional payoff of the conjunctive layer specifically arises **when the feature layer alone is insufficient** (feature-ambiguous problems) — implying feature-layer representations remain available and are used preferentially/sufficiently when problems are NOT feature-ambiguous, and the conjunctive layer becomes behaviorally decisive only when feature overlap is high. This is a coexistence + graded-recruitment account, not a strict replacement account.

**"Explicit-feature" vs "configural" debate:** The task's framing maps onto the real debate in this literature between (a) the Bussey/Saksida/Cowell "representational-hierarchical"/PMFC account (perirhinal computes genuine conjunctive/configural codes as a graded continuation of VVS feature hierarchy, perception-memory continuum, no sharp boundary) and (b) traditional "declarative memory" / MTL-systems accounts (Squire, Zola-Morgan; and separately Suzuki) that treat PRC as doing genuinely different computational work (memory storage/binding for declarative memory) rather than an extension of perceptual feature coding — this is the "perception vs memory," "boxological" systems view Bussey & Saksida 2007 explicitly argue against ("thinking outside of the boxes" title is a direct rhetorical jab at box-and-arrow systems models). This is CONTESTED — the systems-memory camp (Squire et al.) and the representational-hierarchical camp (Bussey/Saksida/Cowell) have an active, decades-long, published disagreement about whether PRC's contribution to memory tasks reflects perceptual/configural representation vs a qualitatively distinct declarative-memory process. I did not find a resolving meta-analysis; treat as CONTESTED / ongoing.

### 3. INTERFERENCE ACCOUNT

**ESTABLISHED framework claim, but quantitative capacity numbers are largely UNPINNED in what I could retrieve.**

- **Cowell, Bussey & Saksida 2006** (J Neurosci, full text retrieved): explicit statement — **"The role of the perirhinal cortex in both visual discrimination and object recognition is the resolution of feature ambiguity, the property of a problem arising when it is difficult to find a solution on the basis of features alone."** The model shows that lesioning the conjunctive layer (simulating PRC damage) selectively impairs performance specifically as feature ambiguity/feature overlap between stimuli increases, reproducing the empirical rat-lesion pattern (Bartko et al. 2007) and human amnesia perceptual-oddity deficits. This is the "object-level vs feature-level interference" account: interference is framed as arising from overlapping FEATURE-level representations shared across multiple objects; the conjunctive/PRC layer resolves this by creating unique, higher-order codes that do not overlap even when constituent features do.
- I explicitly attempted but could **NOT extract quantitative model outputs** (percent correct, d-prime, or "number of items before interference sets in") from the Cowell 2006 J Neurosci full text via my available fetch — the WebFetch tool reported: "no explicit d-prime, percent correct, or numerical capacity measures... Results are presented graphically (Figures 4–6)... without specific performance thresholds or capacity limits quantified [in the extractable text]." **Flag: this may be a limitation of my HTML/text extraction (numbers may live in figures/tables not captured by the fetch tool) rather than a true absence in the paper — I could not view the figures directly.** I am NOT asserting the paper contains no numbers; I am asserting I could not pin numbers from this scan. Treat capacity/quantitative content of this specific paper as **UNPINNED BY THIS SCAN** (not necessarily unpinned in the literature).
- **Bartko, S.J., Winters, B.D., Cowell, R.A., Saksida, L.M., & Bussey, T.J. (2007).** "Perceptual functions of perirhinal cortex in rats: zero-delay object recognition and simultaneous oddity discriminations." *Journal of Neuroscience*, 27(10), 2548–2559. DOI 10.1523/JNEUROSCI.5171-06.2007. PMCID PMC6672512 (empirical, not a model paper). Retrieved qualitative results: discrimination-ratio metric used (not percent-correct); in the "low" feature-overlap condition both lesioned and control rats performed similarly (no significant difference); in the "high" feature-overlap condition, perirhinal+postrhinal (PPRh) lesioned rats' discrimination ratio fell to/below zero (chance or below), i.e., a qualitative interference-driven collapse specifically under high feature ambiguity, absent under low ambiguity. Simultaneous-oddity task: lesioned rats showed reduced oddity-preference scores specifically in the high-perceptual-difficulty condition. **I could not extract the exact discrimination-ratio numeric values (e.g., mean ± SEM) from the fetch** — tag as ESTABLISHED qualitative pattern, UNPINNED exact numbers in this scan.
- **Kent et al. 2016** (Neurobiol Learn Mem): frames PRC's conjunctive coding explicitly as a form of "pattern separation" (interference reduction) mechanism generalized beyond hippocampal spatial pattern separation — i.e., explicitly analogizes PRC feature-conjunction coding to hippocampal DG/CA3 pattern-separation computations, both serving to "reduce overlap between similar input patterns to minimize interference amongst stored representations." This is the clearest explicit bridge in the literature between "conjunctive code" and "interference reduction," stated as a general principle rather than with a specific capacity number.

**Bottom line on numbers:** across everything I could access in this scan, I found **NO explicit quantitative statement** (in the accessible text) of "a conjunctive code buys N more discriminable items" or a stated capacity/d-prime improvement figure comparing feature-only vs conjunctive coding. This should be reported as **UNPINNED** — the field states the qualitative mechanism (conjunctive code resolves feature ambiguity / reduces interference) repeatedly and consistently, but a hard capacity number is not something I could verify exists, let alone retrieve.

### 4. ADDITIVE vs CONJUNCTIVE — HEAD-TO-HEAD NUMBERS

**No head-to-head numeric contrast found within the Cowell/Bussey/Saksida perirhinal literature itself** (the two-layer model uses parallel/averaged output, not a numerically reported additive-vs-conjunctive accuracy comparison that I could extract). This part is **UNPINNED** for the perirhinal-specific literature in this scan.

The mathematically adjacent **configural-vs-elemental associative-learning literature**, however, does have explicit, decades-old quantitative head-to-heads:

- **Rescorla, R.A. & Wagner, A.R. (1972)** elemental model: associative strength of a compound = linear sum of the strengths of its constituent elements (classic Rescorla-Wagner rule). ESTABLISHED, foundational.
- **Pearce, J.M. (1987, 1994)** configural model: a compound stimulus (e.g., AB) is represented as a unique, unitary configural cue, not decomposable into A+B; associative strength for the compound accrues independently of A and B, and generalizes only partially to A or B alone (via a similarity function). ESTABLISHED as the named contrasting theory.
- **Unique-cue theory** (Rescorla 1972 patterning paper; Whitlow & Wagner 1972): a middle-ground elemental-compatible account — represents compound AB as "ABX" where X is an additional (unobserved) unique configural element added onto elemental summation, allowing elemental math to still solve negative patterning. ESTABLISHED as a named alternative resolving the same data pattern via a different mechanism (still fundamentally additive/elemental, with an added unique-cue term).
- **Negative patterning (A+, B+, AB−):** ESTABLISHED empirical phenomenon (widely replicated across species — rats, pigeons, honeybees per the Complex Olfactory Learning paper retrieved, humans) — animals/humans learn to respond to A alone and B alone but withhold responding to the AB compound. This pattern is mathematically impossible for a *pure*, standard Rescorla-Wagner elemental model without a unique-cue addition (a stated, essentially provable, mathematical result — pure summation model cannot produce AB<A,B at asymptote without extra machinery), and is natively predicted by Pearce's configural model. However, as the search directly returned: **"successful negative-patterning discrimination can only determine that a traditional elemental Rescorla-Wagner account (without a unique cue) cannot explain it, but cannot dissociate between Pearce's configural theory [and] Wagner and Rescorla's unique-cue theory."** — i.e., negative patterning alone does NOT cleanly discriminate configural-only vs elemental+unique-cue accounts. Tag: ESTABLISHED but the theoretical DISSOCIATION between accounts from this single phenomenon is explicitly stated as impossible — a genuine, literature-acknowledged ambiguity.
- **Myers, K.M., Vogel, E.H., Shin, J., & Wagner, A.R. (2001).** "A comparison of the Rescorla-Wagner and Pearce models in a negative patterning and a summation problem." *Animal Learning & Behavior* (later *Learning & Behavior*), volume/pages (I was blocked by paywall/login walls from directly re-confirming exact volume/page numbers beyond what search snippets gave — flag as **SECONDARY-SOURCE-derived citation, not independently verified page range**; search snippets indicate this is a Springer/*Animal Learning & Behavior* 2001 article, DOI 10.3758/BF03192814). Design: A+/B+/C+/AB+/AC+/BC+/ABC− in rabbit eyeblink conditioning. **Explicit head-to-head numeric-direction predictions** (from what I could retrieve — actual magnitude numbers/percent-CR values were NOT retrievable due to paywall, so treat the exact numbers as UNPINNED, but the qualitative directional predictions ARE established from the abstract/secondary text):
  - Experiment 1: Rescorla-Wagner predicts response(AB, AC, BC) > response(A, B, C) at asymptote; Pearce predicts the OPPOSITE ordering. Result: rabbit eyelid-conditioning data supported Rescorla-Wagner's (elemental) direction — contrasted explicitly against earlier pigeon autoshaping data that had supported Pearce's (configural) direction. This is a genuine SPECIES/PREPARATION-DEPENDENT split in which model wins — flag explicitly as **CONTESTED across paradigms** (rabbit eyeblink favors elemental; pigeon autoshaping favors configural) rather than a clean universal winner.
  - Experiment 2: response to novel ABC compound predicted by Rescorla-Wagner to be greater when trained on A+/B+/C+ than when trained on AB+/AC+/BC+; Pearce predicts the opposite. (Directional predictions retrieved; magnitude numbers not retrieved — UNPINNED exact numbers.)
- **Harris, J.A. (2006).** "Elemental representations of stimuli in associative learning." *Psychological Review*, 113(3), 584–605. (Full citation given in the file path itself, content blocked by 403 on fetch — **UNVERIFIED beyond title/citation**, could not extract content in this scan.) This is a known review proposing a "unique-cue"-style elemental-representation account reconciling much configural-looking data within an elemental framework — cite as existing but UNVERIFIED CONTENT in this scan.

**Overall verdict on Q4:** The elemental-vs-configural literature is long-standing, has clean qualitative directional head-to-head predictions that have been tested (Myers et al. 2001), and shows a **paradigm-dependent split** (rabbit eyeblink data favor elemental/Rescorla-Wagner; pigeon autoshaping data favor configural/Pearce) rather than a universal winner — this is the closest real quantitative-flavored analogue to the "additive vs conjunctive" contrast the task asks about, but I could NOT retrieve the actual percent-conditioned-response magnitude numbers (paywalled) — report the directional/qualitative result as ESTABLISHED-SINGLE-STUDY-level and flag magnitude numbers as UNPINNED IN THIS SCAN.
